messages:
Jane Lee (Acme): Hey team — our March invoice has a ~3x jump vs what the dashboard shows for tokens. Org acme-123, invoice INV-2026-03. Small sample: req_1943211001, req_1943211102, req_1943211150 between 2026-03-15 14:05-14:08 UTC. We're using continuous batching + KV prefetch. Dashboard shows ~100 tokens, invoice shows ~320. Can someone explain?

Tara Nguyen: Sorry about that, we'll investigate. Can you paste a couple full request IDs + the timezone window and whether you had prefetch/auto-batching on (sounds like yes)?

Jane Lee (Acme): IDs above. Prefetch=on, continuous batching enabled (batch_window_ms=40). Payloads are short: system ~80 tokens, user ~20, no long generations.

Sam Ortiz: Thanks. From billing side we'll pull meter_events for those req ids/time range. @Rahul @Zoe can you run a quick check on meter pipeline and batch traces for acme-123?

Rahul Patel: Quick summary: looks like "cache shadowing" due to prefetch + continuous batching. Metering currently records billed tokens when request is enqueued into the batch. If a KV/prefix cache later supplies the prefix (cache hit), the actual served tokens drop but the billed tokens reflect the earlier estimate. That mismatch explains served_vs_billed gaps when lots of requests later hit the cache.

Zoe Kim: Exactly. Batch builder estimates full context at enqueue time. Prefetch will then populate KV cache and subsequent requests in same batch or shortly after may get prefix hits, reducing served tokens. Meter counts don't backfill based on post-serve cache hits. We're tracking this as a correctness gap.

Jane Lee (Acme): So we're being charged for tokens that never actually hit the model? That feels wrong.

Tara Nguyen: I hear you. Short-term options: 1) disable prefetch, or 2) reduce batch_window_ms so enqueue-time overestimates are smaller. Engineering is evaluating changing metering to record on-response for cacheable prefixes but that's a larger change. Sam — billing, can you advise on credits?

Sam Ortiz: We'll triage credits per account. Please provide full invoice number, exact time window, and traffic samples (you already provided a few request IDs which helps). We'll hold actions until eng confirms repro reproducible.

Rahul Patel: For internal repro (and what to run to validate): 1) enable continuous batching with batch_window_ms ~40 and prefetch=on. 2) seed KV cache with a shared prefix P and short TTL (~5s) so prefetch will populate then subsequent requests hit the cache. 3) flood 100–200 concurrent short requests that share prefix P. 4) query meter events:

```sql
SELECT request_id, meter_phase, billed_tokens, served_tokens, event_ts
FROM meter_events
WHERE org_id='acme-123'
  AND event_ts BETWEEN '2026-03-15T14:04:00Z' AND '2026-03-15T14:09:00Z'
  AND request_id IN ('req_1943211001','req_1943211102','req_1943211150');
```

You should see rows where billed_tokens > served_tokens. Also check trace field `continuous_batching.batch_builder_estimate` and `kv_prefetch.hit` in the span logs.

Zoe Kim: Workarounds for customers: if possible, set request-level option `metering: "on_response"` (beta) or disable prefetch during heavy high-overlap workloads. I'll link the internal RFC/notes in the follow-up.

Tara Nguyen: Jane — can you try disabling prefetch for 30–60 minutes and re-run the same load? If that closes the gap, billing can take that into account. If you can't toggle, we can repro in our sandbox using your prefix.

Jane Lee (Acme): I can toggle prefetch. Turning off now, will run the same set and report back in ~30m. Thanks.

metering-bot: Metering export job started for org acme-123 range 2026-03-15T14:04:00Z - 2026-03-15T14:10:00Z (job id m-20260315-01).

Sam Ortiz: Got the export job id. If the reproduction confirms the gap, billing will propose a credit workflow. Please keep this thread updated with the disable/enable results and any logs.

Rahul Patel: Note for eng: also inspect `batch_builder.estimate_tokens` vs `serve.actual_tokens` in traces. We should instrument a post-serve reconciliation for cacheable prefixes; that will be ENG-priv-metering backlog.

Zoe Kim: I'll file ENG-priv-metering-2026 and add proposed mitigations + ETA.

Jane Lee (Acme): Quick update — after disabling prefetch and re-running the load for 30m the served vs billed numbers align closely. I can share logs if you want.

Tara Nguyen: Great — thanks for testing. Sam, please proceed with next steps for credits if we confirm delta on invoice. We'll keep this open until eng ticket has an owner.
